prerequisites: Prior knowledge of Graphic Expression is recommended.
It is convenient for students to have notions of sketching, fluent handling of drawing software, and bibliographic research skills.

learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand and apply technological and graphic concepts adapted to new situations for professional development.
Develop strategies and procedures in solving graphic problems as a means to approach engineering projects.
Use graphic communication among technicians, specifically in producing and interpreting standardized technical drawing plans for Industrial Engineering, incorporating new technologies.
Work in a team, where they develop their knowledge with a critical and responsible technical/cultural exchange.
Plan and manage projects in the field of industrial engineering according to current legislation.
Interpret and represent assembly and detail drawings of mechanisms, structures, and installations.
Master and fluently use parametric drawing software.
Determine operating conditions of common parts in mechanisms and the relationship between them.
Correctly use mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards for graphic representation.
Know the industrial design method and its work tools.

syllabus_topics: Installation, environment, and project management in Autodesk Inventor.
Design assistants I: shafts, keys, bearings, pins.
Design assistants II: gears, springs, belts, and chains.
Other environments: Welding, Sheet metal parts.
Shafts and axles, keys and pins.
Other transmission elements: belts and chains.
assessment_rules: Students must attend at least 80% of practical classes; otherwise, they are considered 'not presented' in Ordinary Evaluation. If all established minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as: 0.2 x EV1 + 0.3 x EV2 + 0.3 x EV3 + 0.2 x EV4. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. EV1 and EV3 require a minimum of 50% of their maximum score to sum grades. Grades for passed evaluation systems are retained until the extraordinary evaluation. For extraordinary evaluation, students must repeat theoretical and/or practical exams (EV1 and EV3); those who did not complete group work (EV2) must complete an individual work. Students opting for differentiated evaluation must pass theoretical and practical exams (EV1 and EV3) with a weight of 40% and 60% respectively.
